# Reusable workflow reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-docs.mjs. Edit the manifest, then run `make docs`. -->

Every workflow here is called with `uses:`, not copied. Pin to `@v1` for the moving
major, or to an exact release for a frozen pipeline — see
[VERSIONING.md](VERSIONING.md).

Each one checks this repo out at `job.workflow_sha` so the composite actions it runs
always match the workflow version you pinned. You do not need to do anything for that to
work; it is explained in [CONSUMING.md](CONSUMING.md).

---

## `ai-agent-task`

AI agent task — Issue → agent → pull request. The implementation half of agentic-toolkit's loop, as a

```yaml
jobs:
  ai_agent_task:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/ai-agent-task.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Issue → agent → pull request. The implementation half of agentic-toolkit's loop, as a
reusable workflow.

The caller decides the trigger (a label, a slash command, a dispatch); this workflow
handles running the agent on a fresh branch and getting a PR open. A human stays in the
loop at both ends: someone applies the label, and someone reviews and merges. **The agent
never merges its own work.**

`complexity: high` routes to plan-first: the agent writes an implementation plan to
`docs/plans/` and opens a PR containing only that plan, so the approach gets reviewed
before any code exists. That is the cheapest place to catch a wrong approach.

── Security ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
The agent runs full-auto. `issue-body` is untrusted input written by whoever opened the
issue, so it is passed to the agent as data, never interpolated into a shell command.
The real boundary is the job token: `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`, nothing
more. Never call this from `pull_request_target`. See docs/SECURITY.md.

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | `string` | **yes** | — | The task for the agent. Usually the issue body. Treated as untrusted data. |
| `issue-number` | `string` | no | `""` | Issue this implements; used for `Closes #N` and branch naming. |
| `issue-title` | `string` | no | `""` | Issue title, used in the PR title. |
| `complexity` | `string` | no | `medium` | `low`/`medium` implement directly; `high` writes a plan for approval first. |
| `provider` | `string` | no | `claude` | claude \| openai \| gemini \| aider |
| `model` | `string` | no | `""` | Model override. |
| `default-model` | `string` | no | `sonnet` | Fallback tier when `model` is empty. |
| `max-turns` | `string` | no | `60` | Cap on agent iterations. |
| `base-branch` | `string` | no | `""` | Branch to base the work on. Empty uses the default branch. |
| `branch-prefix` | `string` | no | `agent` | Prefix for the working branch. |
| `conventions-file` | `string` | no | `CLAUDE.md` | Project agent guide the agent must read before starting. |
| `pr-labels` | `string` | no | `agent-generated` | Comma-separated labels applied to the PR. |
| `test-command` | `string` | no | `""` | Command the agent is instructed to run before opening the PR. Empty leaves verification to the agent's own judgement. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `45` | Job timeout — the hard bound on a runaway agent. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | no | — |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | no | — |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | no | — |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | no | — |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | no | — |
| `AGENT_GITHUB_TOKEN` | no | PAT used instead of `GITHUB_TOKEN` when the agent's PR must trigger other workflows. Pushes made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` deliberately do not fire `pull_request`. |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `branch` | The branch the agent worked on. |
| `changed` | `true` if the agent produced changes. |

## `ai-eval`

AI eval — Run an LLM eval suite on every PR and gate the merge on it.

```yaml
jobs:
  ai_eval:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/ai-eval.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Run an LLM eval suite on every PR and gate the merge on it.

This is the missing CI stage for anything that ships a prompt. Unit tests tell you the
code around the model works; only an eval tells you the model still does the job after
you reworded the system prompt or bumped the model version.

The baseline flow is what makes it useful over time: the score from the default branch is
fetched (from a committed baseline file or the previous run's artifact) and the PR is
failed on a *regression*, not just on an absolute threshold. That catches the slow
erosion that a fixed threshold set generously at the start will never notice.

Provider keys reach the suite through `provider-keys`, a `ENV_NAME=SECRET_NAME` mapping,
so this workflow never has to know whether you use OpenRouter, Anthropic, or a local
vLLM endpoint.

Usage:
  jobs:
    eval:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/ai-eval.yml@v1
      with:
        threshold: '90'
        max-regression: '2'
        provider-keys: |
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=OPENROUTER_API_KEY
      secrets: inherit

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runner` | `string` | no | `promptfoo` | promptfoo \| custom |
| `config` | `string` | no | `promptfooconfig.yaml` | promptfoo config file. |
| `command` | `string` | no | `""` | Command for `runner: custom`. Must write the results file. |
| `results-file` | `string` | no | `eval-results.json` | Results JSON path. |
| `pass-rate-jq` | `string` | no | `[(.results.stats.successes // 0), (.results.stats.failures // 0)]` | jq expression returning `[passes, failures]` from the results file. |
| `threshold` | `string` | no | `100` | Minimum pass rate percentage. |
| `max-regression` | `string` | no | `0` | Allowed drop in percentage points versus the baseline. |
| `baseline-file` | `string` | no | `""` | Committed baseline score (`{"pass_rate": 92.5}`). Empty falls back to the baseline artifact published by the last run on the default branch. |
| `publish-baseline` | `boolean` | no | `false` | 'true to publish this run''s score as the new baseline artifact. Callers should set this only on the default branch — publishing from a PR would let a regression rewrite the baseline it was supposed to be measured against.' |
| `max-cost-usd` | `string` | no | `""` | Abort if the suite costs more than this. |
| `concurrency-limit` | `string` | no | `4` | Parallel eval requests. |
| `cache` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to let promptfoo reuse cached responses for unchanged cases. |
| `python` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to set up Python (for a pytest/DeepEval-style custom runner). |
| `node` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to set up Node (needed by promptfoo). |
| `provider-keys` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `ENV_NAME=SECRET_NAME` mappings for model API keys. |
| `working-directory` | `string` | no | `.` | Directory to run in. |
| `comment-on-pr` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to post the score as a sticky PR comment. |
| `fail-on-threshold` | `boolean` | no | `true` | false to report the score without failing the check. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `30` | Job timeout. |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `pass-rate` | The pass rate percentage. |
| `passed` | `true` if the suite met the threshold and regression budget. |
| `cost-usd` | Reported cost, when available. |

## `ai-pr-review`

AI PR review — Automated PR review by whichever agent the repo is configured for. Opt-in and cost-aware

```yaml
jobs:
  ai_pr_review:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/ai-pr-review.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Automated PR review by whichever agent the repo is configured for. Opt-in and cost-aware
by design.

It posts one review comment per PR, edited in place on re-runs. It never pushes code (the
job token is `contents: read`) and never approves or merges — a human owns that.

── Cost levers, all on by default ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  • `synchronize` is NOT a trigger. It fires on every push to an open PR, and leaving it
    in re-runs a full review per commit — the dominant cost driver by a wide margin.
    Reviews happen on open, reopen, and ready-for-review. Re-trigger by closing/reopening.
  • Drafts are skipped: reviewing work-in-progress spends tokens on code about to change.
  • Docs-only and lockfile-only PRs are skipped via `paths-ignore` at the caller.
  • Dependabot is skipped — its runs use the Dependabot secret store, which does not
    expose Actions secrets, so the job can only ever fail with a 401.
  • Fork PRs are skipped for the same reason: no secrets under `pull_request`.
  • `concurrency` cancels a superseded review so you only pay for the latest.
  • The model is a parameter; `sonnet` is the default because it catches PR-level
    correctness and cleanup issues at a fraction of the cost of a frontier tier.

Usage:
  jobs:
    review:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/ai-pr-review.yml@v1
      with:
        provider: claude
      secrets: inherit

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | `string` | no | `claude` | claude \| openai \| gemini \| aider |
| `model` | `string` | no | `""` | Model override. Empty uses `default-model`. |
| `default-model` | `string` | no | `sonnet` | Fallback tier: `haiku` cheapest, `sonnet` balanced, `opus` deepest. |
| `max-turns` | `string` | no | `25` | Cap on agent iterations, bounding a runaway review. |
| `use-code-review-plugin` | `boolean` | no | `false` | 'true to run Anthropic''s `/code-review` plugin instead of the built-in prompt. Claude only; produces inline comments on specific lines.' |
| `focus` | `string` | no | `""` | Extra review instructions appended to the prompt. |
| `conventions-file` | `string` | no | `CLAUDE.md` | Project agent guide the reviewer is told to read first. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `15` | Job timeout — a hard bound on spend. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | no | — |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | no | — |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | no | — |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | no | — |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | no | — |

### Outputs

_No outputs._

## `cloudformation`

CloudFormation — CloudFormation change set on PRs, execute on merge — the same review gate the Terraform

```yaml
jobs:
  cloudformation:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/cloudformation.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

CloudFormation change set on PRs, execute on merge — the same review gate the Terraform
workflow gives you, for stacks CloudFormation owns.

`mode` picks the half:
  change-set → create the change set, comment the resource diff, leave it unexecuted
  execute    → execute a change set created earlier, by name
  deploy     → change set and execute in one run
  delete     → tear the stack down (for ephemeral PR environments)

Multiple stacks run from one call via the `stacks` matrix input, so an app with a
network, data, and service stack deploys in a defined order rather than three copies of
this job.

Linting is a separate job: `cfn-lint` catches the class of error that a change set can't,
because a template with a bad intrinsic function never gets far enough to produce one.

Usage:
  jobs:
    plan:
      if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/cloudformation.yml@v1
      with:
        mode: change-set
        stack-name: my-api
        template: infra/api.yaml
        aws-region: us-east-1
        aws-role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gha-cfn-plan
      permissions: { contents: read, pull-requests: write, id-token: write }

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `string` | no | `change-set` | change-set \| execute \| deploy \| delete |
| `stack-name` | `string` | no | `""` | Stack name. Ignored when `stacks` is set. |
| `template` | `string` | no | `""` | Template path or S3 URL. Ignored when `stacks` is set. |
| `stacks` | `string` | no | `""` | JSON array of stack objects for a multi-stack deploy, e.g. `[{"stack-name":"net","template":"infra/net.yaml"},{"stack-name":"api","template":"infra/api.yaml"}]`. Each object may carry `parameters`, `capabilities`, and `tags` overrides. Deployed strictly in order — a service stack that imports a network stack's exports must not race it. |
| `parameters` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `Key=Value` parameters applied to every stack. |
| `parameters-file` | `string` | no | `""` | JSON parameters file in the AWS CLI shape. |
| `capabilities` | `string` | no | `CAPABILITY_IAM` | Comma-separated capabilities. |
| `tags` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `Key=Value` tags. |
| `change-set-name` | `string` | no | `""` | Change set name. Set the same value on the `change-set` and `execute` runs so the second executes exactly what the first produced. |
| `role-arn` | `string` | no | `""` | CloudFormation service role ARN. |
| `package` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to `aws cloudformation package` before deploying (SAM, large templates). |
| `s3-bucket` | `string` | no | `""` | Bucket for packaged artifacts. |
| `fail-on-replacement` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to fail when the change set would replace any resource. |
| `termination-protection` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to enable termination protection after a successful deploy. |
| `lint` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run cfn-lint over `lint-paths` before touching AWS. |
| `lint-paths` | `string` | no | `infra/**/*.yaml infra/**/*.yml infra/**/*.json` | Space-separated template globs for cfn-lint. |
| `lint-ignore` | `string` | no | `""` | Comma-separated cfn-lint rule IDs to ignore, e.g. `W3011,W2001`. |
| `guard` | `boolean` | no | `false` | 'true to run cfn-guard policy checks. Needs `guard-rules`; enforces org policy (encryption, no public buckets) that cfn-lint does not cover.' |
| `guard-rules` | `string` | no | `""` | Path to a cfn-guard rules file or directory. |
| `aws-region` | `string` | **yes** | — | AWS region. |
| `aws-role-to-assume` | `string` | no | `""` | OIDC role ARN. Preferred over static keys. |
| `environment-name` | `string` | no | `""` | GitHub Environment gating the deploy (where approval rules live). |
| `comment-on-pr` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to post the change set as a sticky PR comment. |
| `notify` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to send a Slack/Discord notification. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `60` | Per-job timeout. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | no | Static access key, used only when no OIDC role is given. |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | no | Static secret key. |
| `CFN_SECRET_PARAMETERS` | no | Newline-separated `Key=Value` stack parameters that must not appear in `with:`. Merged over `parameters`. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK` | no | — |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK` | no | — |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `has-changes` | `true` if any stack had changes. |
| `outputs-json` | The last deployed stack's outputs as JSON. |

## `deploy-aws`

Deploy AWS — One AWS deploy workflow, three targets, selected by `target`.

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy_aws:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

One AWS deploy workflow, three targets, selected by `target`.

  ecs    → register a task definition with the new image and roll the service
  lambda → update the function and move an alias to the new published version
  static → sync a build directory to S3 with correct cache headers, invalidate CloudFront

One workflow rather than three because everything around the deploy — OIDC auth,
environment gating, notification, rollback reporting — is identical, and keeping it in
one place means a fix to the auth path fixes all three.

Authentication is OIDC by default; `aws-role-to-assume` is all you need. See
docs/SECURITY.md for the trust policy.

Usage:
  jobs:
    deploy:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml@v1
      with:
        target: ecs
        aws-region: us-east-1
        aws-role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::1234:role/gha-deploy
        cluster: prod
        service: api
        image: ${{ needs.image.outputs.image-digest-ref }}
        environment-name: production
      permissions:
        contents: read
        id-token: write

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | `string` | **yes** | — | ecs \| lambda \| static |
| `aws-region` | `string` | **yes** | — | AWS region. |
| `aws-role-to-assume` | `string` | no | `""` | OIDC role ARN. Preferred over static keys. |
| `environment-name` | `string` | no | `""` | GitHub Environment to deploy through (where approval rules live). |
| `cluster` | `string` | no | `""` | ECS cluster. |
| `service` | `string` | no | `""` | ECS service. |
| `container-name` | `string` | no | `""` | Container to update. Empty targets the first one. |
| `task-definition-file` | `string` | no | `""` | Committed task definition to use as the base. Empty fetches the live one. |
| `wait-for-stability` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to block until the ECS service is stable. |
| `function-name` | `string` | no | `""` | Lambda function name. |
| `alias` | `string` | no | `""` | Lambda alias to move to the new version. |
| `zip-file` | `string` | no | `""` | Local deployment zip, as an alternative to an image. |
| `source` | `string` | no | `""` | Local directory to publish. |
| `bucket` | `string` | no | `""` | Target S3 bucket. |
| `prefix` | `string` | no | `""` | Key prefix within the bucket. |
| `distribution-id` | `string` | no | `""` | CloudFront distribution to invalidate. |
| `artifact-name` | `string` | no | `""` | Build artifact to download before a static deploy. Use this when a separate build job produced the output — it avoids rebuilding just to publish. |
| `image` | `string` | no | `""` | Image to deploy for `ecs`/`lambda`. Prefer an immutable digest ref. |
| `environment-variables` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `KEY=value` pairs applied to the deployed workload. |
| `notify` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to send a Slack/Discord notification. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `30` | Job timeout. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | no | Static access key. Only used when no OIDC role is given. |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | no | Static secret key. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK` | no | — |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK` | no | — |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `target` | The deploy target that ran. |
| `result` | A target-specific identifier — task definition ARN, Lambda version, or bucket URI. |

## `deploy-fly`

Deploy Fly.io — Deploy to Fly.io, with first-class support for per-PR ephemeral apps.

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy_fly:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/deploy-fly.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Deploy to Fly.io, with first-class support for per-PR ephemeral apps.

Set `app-suffix: -pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}` and
`create-if-missing: true` and every PR gets its own app and URL. Pair it with
`destroy-on-close` in a `pull_request: [closed]` job so those apps don't accumulate —
forgotten preview apps are the main way a Fly bill grows without anyone noticing.

Usage:
  jobs:
    deploy:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/deploy-fly.yml@v1
      with:
        app: my-api
        image: ${{ needs.image.outputs.image-digest-ref }}
      secrets: inherit

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | `string` | no | `""` | Fly app name. Empty reads it from the config file. |
| `app-suffix` | `string` | no | `""` | Appended to the app name, e.g. `-pr-42`. |
| `config` | `string` | no | `fly.toml` | Fly config file. |
| `working-directory` | `string` | no | `.` | Directory to run flyctl from. |
| `image` | `string` | no | `""` | Pre-built image to deploy. Empty builds remotely from the Dockerfile. |
| `strategy` | `string` | no | `rolling` | immediate \| rolling \| bluegreen \| canary |
| `region` | `string` | no | `""` | Primary region for a newly created app. |
| `org` | `string` | no | `personal` | Fly organization. |
| `create-if-missing` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to create the app when it does not exist. Needed for per-PR apps. |
| `destroy-on-close` | `boolean` | no | `false` | 'true to destroy the app instead of deploying. Call this from a `pull_request: [closed]` job to clean up an ephemeral preview app.' |
| `environment-name` | `string` | no | `""` | GitHub Environment to deploy through. |
| `secrets-map` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `FLY_SECRET_NAME=GH_SECRET_NAME` mappings, staged on the app before the deploy so they ship in the same release. |
| `comment-on-pr` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to post the app URL as a sticky PR comment. |
| `notify` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to send a Slack/Discord notification. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `30` | Job timeout. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FLY_API_TOKEN` | **yes** | Fly API token. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK` | no | — |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK` | no | — |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `app` | The resolved app name. |
| `url` | The app URL. |

## `deploy-gcp`

Deploy GCP — Deploy to Google Cloud — Cloud Run today, with the same auth/gating/notify shell as the

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy_gcp:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/deploy-gcp.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Deploy to Google Cloud — Cloud Run today, with the same auth/gating/notify shell as the
AWS workflow so switching clouds doesn't mean relearning the pipeline.

Canary support is built in rather than bolted on: set `traffic-percent` and the revision
lands with no traffic, then takes that share. A follow-up `promote` run (traffic-percent
empty) moves the rest over once you're satisfied, and doing nothing rolls back by simply
leaving the old revision serving.

Authentication is Workload Identity Federation by default — no service-account JSON key.

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | `string` | no | `cloud-run` | cloud-run \| static |
| `project-id` | `string` | no | `""` | GCP project. |
| `region` | `string` | no | `us-central1` | Region for the service. |
| `workload-identity-provider` | `string` | no | `""` | WIF provider resource name. Preferred over a service-account key. |
| `service-account` | `string` | no | `""` | Service account to impersonate via WIF. |
| `environment-name` | `string` | no | `""` | GitHub Environment to deploy through. |
| `service` | `string` | no | `""` | Cloud Run service name. |
| `image` | `string` | no | `""` | Container image. Prefer an immutable digest ref. |
| `env-vars` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `KEY=value` environment variables. |
| `secret-refs` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `KEY=secret-name:version` Secret Manager mappings. |
| `runtime-service-account` | `string` | no | `""` | Runtime service account for the revision. |
| `min-instances` | `string` | no | `""` | Minimum instances. |
| `max-instances` | `string` | no | `""` | Maximum instances. |
| `cpu` | `string` | no | `""` | CPU allocation. |
| `memory` | `string` | no | `""` | Memory allocation. |
| `allow-unauthenticated` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to make the service public. |
| `traffic-percent` | `string` | no | `""` | Share of traffic for the new revision. Empty means 100% immediately; a number deploys with no traffic and then migrates that percentage (canary). |
| `source` | `string` | no | `""` | Local directory to publish for `target: static`. |
| `bucket` | `string` | no | `""` | Target GCS bucket URI, e.g. `gs://my-site`. |
| `notify` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to send a Slack/Discord notification. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `30` | Job timeout. |

| Secret | Required | Description |

| `GCP_CREDENTIALS_JSON` | no | Service-account key, used only when no WIF provider is given. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK` | no | — |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK` | no | — |

## `deploy-supabase`

Deploy Supabase — Supabase deploys: migrations, Edge Functions, and project config.

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy_supabase:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Supabase deploys: migrations, Edge Functions, and project config.

The intended pairing is two calls. On a PR, `dry-run: true` posts the pending migrations
as a comment so a schema change gets reviewed like code. On merge, the same workflow runs
for real. Database migrations are the least reversible thing most apps do — reviewing the
diff before it lands is worth the extra job.

Usage:
  jobs:
    plan:
      if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml@v1
      with: { dry-run: true }
      secrets: inherit

    apply:
      if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml@v1
      with: { functions: all, environment-name: production }
      secrets: inherit

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `migrate` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run `supabase db push`. |
| `functions` | `string` | no | `""` | `all`, a comma-separated list of function names, or empty to skip. |
| `config` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to push `supabase/config.toml`. |
| `seed` | `string` | no | `""` | SQL file applied after migrations. Must be idempotent. |
| `dry-run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to report pending migrations without applying anything. |
| `no-verify-jwt` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to deploy functions with JWT verification off. |
| `function-secrets-map` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `FUNCTION_ENV_NAME=GH_SECRET_NAME` mappings set on the project before functions deploy. |
| `working-directory` | `string` | no | `.` | Directory containing `supabase/`. |
| `environment-name` | `string` | no | `""` | GitHub Environment to deploy through. |
| `comment-on-pr` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to post the migration plan/result as a sticky PR comment. |
| `notify` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to send a Slack/Discord notification. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `20` | Job timeout. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` | **yes** | Supabase account access token. |
| `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` | **yes** | Target project ref. |
| `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` | no | Database password, required for migrations. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK` | no | — |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK` | no | — |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `migrations-applied` | Migration versions applied. |
| `functions-deployed` | Function names deployed. |

## `docker-build`

Docker build — Build a container image, scan it, and push it — the job most deploy pipelines start with.

```yaml
jobs:
  docker_build:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/docker-build.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Build a container image, scan it, and push it — the job most deploy pipelines start with.

The ordering is deliberate: build → scan → push. Scanning before the push means a
critical CVE stops the image from reaching the registry at all, rather than being
discovered after something already pulled it. The cost is that a scan failure means
rebuilding, which is cheap with layer caching.

Registry auth is handled by target: `ghcr` and `dockerhub` log in with a token, `ecr`
runs `aws-auth` with OIDC first, `gar` runs `gcp-auth` with Workload Identity first.

Usage:
  jobs:
    image:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/docker-build.yml@v1
      with:
        registry: ecr
        registry-host: 1234.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
        aws-region: us-east-1
        aws-role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::1234:role/gha-push
      permissions:
        contents: read
        id-token: write

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `registry` | `string` | no | `ghcr` | ghcr \| dockerhub \| ecr \| gar \| custom |
| `registry-host` | `string` | no | `""` | Registry host. Required for `ecr`, `gar`, and `custom`. |
| `image` | `string` | no | `""` | Image path without the host. Defaults to the repository name. |
| `context` | `string` | no | `.` | Build context. |
| `file` | `string` | no | `""` | Dockerfile path. |
| `target` | `string` | no | `""` | Dockerfile stage. |
| `platforms` | `string` | no | `linux/amd64` | Build platforms. |
| `build-args` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `KEY=value` build arguments. Never secrets. |
| `push` | `boolean` | no | `true` | 'true to push. Callers normally set this to `github.event_name != ''pull_request''` so PRs validate the build without publishing.' |
| `extra-tags` | `string` | no | `""` | Extra docker/metadata-action tag rules. |
| `cache` | `string` | no | `gha` | gha \| registry \| none |
| `provenance` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to attach SLSA build provenance. |
| `sbom` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to attach an SBOM. |
| `scan` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run a Trivy scan on the built image before pushing. |
| `scan-severity` | `string` | no | `CRITICAL,HIGH` | Severities that fail the scan. |
| `scan-fail` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to block the push when the scan finds something. |
| `aws-region` | `string` | no | `""` | AWS region, for `ecr`. |
| `aws-role-to-assume` | `string` | no | `""` | OIDC role ARN, for `ecr`. |
| `gcp-workload-identity-provider` | `string` | no | `""` | WIF provider, for `gar`. |
| `gcp-service-account` | `string` | no | `""` | Service account to impersonate, for `gar`. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `45` | Job timeout. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `REGISTRY_USERNAME` | no | Registry username, for `dockerhub` and `custom`. |
| `REGISTRY_PASSWORD` | no | Registry password/token, for `dockerhub` and `custom`. |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `image` | Fully qualified image reference without a tag. |
| `digest` | The image digest (`sha256:…`). |
| `image-digest-ref` | Immutable `host/repo@sha256:…` reference to hand a deploy job. |
| `version` | The primary version tag. |

## `go-ci`

Go CI — Go CI: gofmt gate, vet, golangci-lint, tests with race detection and coverage, and an

Go CI: gofmt gate, vet, golangci-lint, tests with race detection and coverage, and an

| `golangci-lint-version` | `string` | no | `latest` | golangci-lint version. |
| `vet` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run `go vet ./...`. |

## `llm-cost-report`

LLM cost report — Where the money went: LLM spend plus GitHub Actions runner spend, over a window.

```yaml
jobs:
  llm_cost_report:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/llm-cost-report.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Where the money went: LLM spend plus GitHub Actions runner spend, over a window.

The two costs of an AI-assisted repo pull in opposite directions and are usually tracked
in different places (or not at all). This puts both in one scheduled report so the
trade-off is visible — an agent workflow that halves review time but triples runner
minutes is a decision, not an accident.

  • LLM spend comes from the OpenRouter generation API when `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set.
    It is real charged cost, not an estimate.
  • Runner spend is computed from the Actions API: billable minutes per workflow times
    the per-minute rate for the runner OS.

Runs on a schedule (monthly is the useful cadence) or on demand. Output goes to the job
summary and, optionally, a tracking issue that gets updated in place so the history reads
as a single thread.

Usage:
  on:
    schedule: [{ cron: '0 9 1 * *' }]
    workflow_dispatch:
  jobs:
    cost:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/llm-cost-report.yml@v1
      with: { days: 30, issue-number: '12' }
      secrets: inherit

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | `number` | no | `30` | Window in days. |
| `issue-number` | `string` | no | `""` | Issue to post the report to as a sticky comment. Empty posts nowhere. |
| `include-actions-cost` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to include GitHub Actions runner spend. |
| `include-llm-cost` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to include OpenRouter spend (needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`). |
| `linux-rate` | `string` | no | `0.008` | USD per minute for a Linux runner. |
| `windows-rate` | `string` | no | `0.016` | USD per minute for a Windows runner. |
| `macos-rate` | `string` | no | `0.08` | USD per minute for a macOS runner. |
| `notify` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to send a Slack/Discord summary. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | no | OpenRouter key, read-scoped is enough. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK` | no | — |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK` | no | — |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `total-usd` | Combined estimated spend over the window. |

## `ml-pipeline`

ML pipeline — Train → evaluate → register. A reproducible ML pipeline where the artifact that ships is

```yaml
jobs:
  ml_pipeline:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/ml-pipeline.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Train → evaluate → register. A reproducible ML pipeline where the artifact that ships is
tied to the commit and data that produced it.

The shape:
  1. Pull the dataset from durable storage (S3/GCS/HF) — never from an ad-hoc URL, so the
     inputs are as pinned as the code.
  2. Run training. Optionally restore a previous checkpoint so long runs can resume.
  3. Run evaluation and read a metric out of the results JSON.
  4. Register the model — but only if the metric cleared the gate. A model that got worse
     does not get published, which is the whole point of putting this in CI.

Step 4's gate is what separates this from a shell script. The registered artifact carries
a manifest with per-file checksums and the producing commit, so "which code and data made
the weights currently in prod?" has an answer.

GPU runs: point `runs-on` at a self-hosted or larger runner label. Nothing here assumes
a specific accelerator.

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset-uri` | `string` | no | `""` | Dataset to pull, e.g. `s3://bucket/datasets/v3` or `hf://org/dataset`. |
| `dataset-path` | `string` | no | `data` | Local path the dataset is downloaded to. |
| `checkpoint-uri` | `string` | no | `""` | Checkpoint to resume from. Empty trains from scratch. |
| `checkpoint-path` | `string` | no | `checkpoints` | Local path for the restored checkpoint. |
| `train-command` | `string` | no | `""` | Training command. Empty skips training (eval-only runs). |
| `eval-command` | `string` | no | `""` | Evaluation command. Must write `metrics-file`. |
| `metrics-file` | `string` | no | `metrics.json` | JSON file the eval writes its metrics to. |
| `metric-jq` | `string` | no | `.accuracy` | jq expression selecting the gating metric, e.g. `.accuracy`. |
| `metric-threshold` | `string` | no | `""` | Minimum metric value required to register. Empty disables the gate. |
| `metric-direction` | `string` | no | `higher` | `higher` (accuracy, F1) or `lower` (loss, WER, perplexity). |
| `model-path` | `string` | no | `model` | Local directory holding the trained model to register. |
| `registry-uri` | `string` | no | `""` | Where the model is published on success, e.g. `s3://bucket/models/my-model` or `hf://org/my-model`. Empty skips registration. |
| `hf-repo-type` | `string` | no | `model` | `model` \| `dataset` \| `space`, for a Hugging Face registry URI. |
| `python-version` | `string` | no | `3.12` | Python version. |
| `installer` | `string` | no | `uv` | uv \| pip |
| `groups` | `string` | no | `--all-extras --dev` | Dependency groups/extras. |
| `working-directory` | `string` | no | `.` | Directory to run in. |
| `aws-region` | `string` | no | `""` | AWS region, when the URIs are `s3://`. |
| `aws-role-to-assume` | `string` | no | `""` | OIDC role ARN for S3 access. |
| `gcp-workload-identity-provider` | `string` | no | `""` | WIF provider, when the URIs are `gs://`. |
| `gcp-service-account` | `string` | no | `""` | Service account to impersonate for GCS. |
| `env-map` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `KEY=SECRET_NAME` mappings for training/eval. |
| `public-env` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `KEY=value` non-secret config (hyperparameters). |
| `comment-on-pr` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to post the metrics as a sticky PR comment. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. Point this at a GPU runner for real training. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `360` | Job timeout. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `HF_TOKEN` | no | Hugging Face token, for `hf://` URIs. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK` | no | — |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK` | no | — |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `metric` | The gating metric value that was measured. |
| `registered` | `true` if the model cleared the gate and was published. |

## `node-ci`

Node CI — Node/TypeScript CI: lint + format gate, unit tests with coverage, build, and an optional

```yaml
jobs:
  node_ci:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/node-ci.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Node/TypeScript CI: lint + format gate, unit tests with coverage, build, and an optional
Playwright e2e stage. Modelled on the pipeline running in threaditate.

Usage:
  jobs:
    ci:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/node-ci.yml@v1
      with:
        node-version: '22'
        e2e: auto
        build-env: |
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
      secrets: inherit

── Three things worth knowing ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. `.toolkit` checkout. A reusable workflow cannot `uses: ./actions/…` — inside a called
   workflow `./` is the *caller's* checkout. Each job therefore clones this repo at
   `job.workflow_sha`, the SHA of this very workflow file, so the actions always match
   the workflow version the caller pinned.

2. The format gate runs the formatter and fails if it changed anything, rather than
   running `--check`. Same signal, but the job log then names the offending files.
   Lockfiles are excluded: Dependabot installs regenerate them, which has nothing to do
   with whether code was formatted.

3. `build-env` maps your secret names onto the env var names your build expects, so this
   workflow never has to know either. It requires `secrets: inherit` — without it, the
   `secrets` context here holds only the two secrets declared below.

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node-version` | `string` | no | `22` | Node version. |
| `package-manager` | `string` | no | `auto` | auto \| pnpm \| npm \| yarn \| bun |
| `pnpm-version` | `string` | no | `""` | pnpm version. Empty reads `packageManager` from package.json. |
| `working-directory` | `string` | no | `.` | Directory containing the project. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `lint-command` | `string` | no | `lint` | Lint command, run via the package manager. Empty skips linting. |
| `format-command` | `string` | no | `format` | Formatter command run in write mode; the job fails if it changed tracked files. Empty skips the format gate. |
| `format-ignore` | `string` | no | `:!pnpm-lock.yaml :!package-lock.json :!yarn.lock :!bun.lock :!bun.lockb` | Pathspecs excluded from the format diff check. |
| `typecheck-command` | `string` | no | `""` | Type-check command. Empty skips it. |
| `test-command` | `string` | no | `test:ci` | Unit test command. Empty skips tests. |
| `build-command` | `string` | no | `build` | Build command. Empty skips the build. |
| `coverage` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to upload coverage to Codecov. |
| `coverage-file` | `string` | no | `./coverage/lcov.info` | Coverage file to upload. |
| `e2e` | `string` | no | `none` | Playwright stage: `none`, `smoke` (only @smoke-tagged specs), `full`, or `auto` — smoke on pull requests, full on everything else. |
| `e2e-command` | `string` | no | `exec playwright test --project=chromium {grep}` | Playwright command; `{grep}` is replaced by the tag filter. |
| `e2e-browsers` | `string` | no | `chromium` | Browsers installed for Playwright. |
| `build-env` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `KEY=SECRET_NAME` mappings. Each named secret is exported under `KEY` (masked) for the build, test, and e2e steps. Requires `secrets: inherit`. |
| `public-env` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `KEY=value` pairs for genuinely non-secret config. |
| `required-env` | `string` | no | `""` | Comma-separated env var names that must resolve, or the job fails. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `20` | Per-job timeout. |
| `upload-build` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to upload the build output as an artifact. |
| `build-output-path` | `string` | no | `dist` | Path uploaded when `upload-build` is true. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CODECOV_TOKEN` | no | Codecov upload token. |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `package-manager` | The package manager that was detected. |

## `python-ci`

Python CI — Python CI: ruff lint + format gate, optional mypy, pytest with coverage, and an optional

```yaml
jobs:
  python_ci:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/python-ci.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Python CI: ruff lint + format gate, optional mypy, pytest with coverage, and an optional
version matrix.

uv-first, because in CI the install step is most of the wall clock and uv removes it.
ruff replaces flake8/isort/black with one tool, which is why lint and format are separate
commands against the same binary rather than three jobs.

Usage:
  jobs:
    ci:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/python-ci.yml@v1
      with:
        python-versions: '["3.11","3.12","3.13"]'
        mypy: true
      secrets: inherit

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `python-version` | `string` | no | `3.12` | Python version when not using a matrix. |
| `python-versions` | `string` | no | `""` | JSON array of versions to test against, e.g. `["3.11","3.12"]`. Overrides `python-version` and fans the test job out into a matrix. |
| `installer` | `string` | no | `uv` | uv \| pip |
| `groups` | `string` | no | `--all-extras --dev` | Dependency groups/extras for `uv sync`. |

| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `lint` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run `ruff check`. |
| `lint-command` | `string` | no | `ruff check .` | Override the lint command. |
| `format` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run `ruff format --check`. |
| `format-command` | `string` | no | `ruff format --check --diff .` | Override the format-check command. |
| `mypy` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to run mypy. |
| `mypy-command` | `string` | no | `mypy .` | Override the type-check command. |
| `test-command` | `string` | no | `pytest -q --cov --cov-report=xml --cov-report=term-missing` | Test command. Empty skips tests. |
| `coverage` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to upload coverage to Codecov. |

## `release-please`

Release Please — Conventional-commit releases via release-please, with the personal-repo auto-merge

```yaml
jobs:
  release_please:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/release-please.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Conventional-commit releases via release-please, with the personal-repo auto-merge
workaround that threaditate needed.

release-please opens a release PR that accumulates changelog entries, then cuts the tag
and GitHub release when that PR merges. On an organization repo you'd let GitHub's
"Allow auto-merge" setting close the loop. Personal repos can't enable that setting, so
`gh pr merge --auto` fails with `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` — this workflow polls the
PR's checks itself and squash-merges when they pass.

Two details that were learned the hard way and are load-bearing:

  • The PR number is parsed in the shell, not in `env:`. When release-please runs without
    opening a PR, `steps.release.outputs.pr` is empty, and `fromJSON('')` is a
    template-validation error that fails the whole workflow even behind an `if:` gate.

  • `gh pr checks --watch --required` exits non-zero both when a required check fails and
    when no required checks are configured at all. Those have to be told apart, or a repo
    with no branch protection can never release.

Usage:
  jobs:
    release:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/release-please.yml@v1
      with:
        release-type: node
      permissions:
        contents: write
        pull-requests: write
        checks: read
        statuses: read
        actions: read

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `release-type` | `string` | no | `simple` | release-please strategy: `node`, `python`, `go`, `rust`, `simple`, `terraform-module`, … |
| `config-file` | `string` | no | `""` | Path to `release-please-config.json` for a manifest-driven release. |
| `manifest-file` | `string` | no | `""` | Path to `.release-please-manifest.json`. |
| `target-branch` | `string` | no | `""` | Branch to release from. |
| `auto-merge` | `boolean` | no | `true` | 'true to poll the release PR''s checks and squash-merge it automatically. Set false when a human should approve every release.' |
| `check-wait-seconds` | `number` | no | `45` | Seconds to wait before polling, so the `pull_request` event has time to register the CI workflow. Polling immediately reports "no checks" and merges early. |
| `move-major-tag` | `boolean` | no | `false` | 'true to force-move a `vN` tag to each release commit. This is what lets consumers pin `@v1` — essential for an actions repo, meaningless for an app.' |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RELEASE_TOKEN` | no | PAT used instead of `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Required if the release commit must trigger other workflows — pushes made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` deliberately do not. |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `release-created` | `true` when a release was cut on this run. |
| `tag-name` | The tag that was created. |
| `version` | The released version, without the leading `v`. |
| `major` | The released major version. |

## `rust-ci`

Rust CI — Rust CI: rustfmt gate, clippy with warnings denied, tests, and an optional MSRV check.

```yaml
jobs:
  rust_ci:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/rust-ci.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Rust CI: rustfmt gate, clippy with warnings denied, tests, and an optional MSRV check.

`clippy -D warnings` is the default because clippy's value collapses if warnings are
advisory — they accumulate until nobody reads them. If that's too strict for an existing
codebase, set `clippy-args` to something narrower rather than turning clippy off.

The MSRV job exists because "it compiles on stable" and "it compiles on the version in
your Cargo.toml `rust-version`" are different claims, and only the second one is a
promise to your users.

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `toolchain` | `string` | no | `stable` | Primary toolchain: `stable`, `nightly`, or a pinned version. |
| `msrv` | `string` | no | `""` | Minimum supported Rust version to also build against. Empty skips it. |
| `working-directory` | `string` | no | `.` | Directory containing Cargo.toml. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `fmt` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run `cargo fmt --check`. |
| `clippy` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run clippy. |
| `clippy-args` | `string` | no | `--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | Arguments passed to clippy. |
| `test-command` | `string` | no | `cargo test --all-features` | Test command. Empty skips tests. |
| `doc-test` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to also run doc tests. |
| `build-command` | `string` | no | `""` | Release build command. Empty skips the build job. |
| `targets` | `string` | no | `""` | Comma-separated cross-compilation targets to install. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `30` | Per-job timeout. |

### Outputs

_No outputs._

## `security-scan`

Security scan — Security scanning: filesystem vulnerabilities, IaC misconfiguration, leaked secrets,

```yaml
jobs:
  security_scan:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/security-scan.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Security scanning: filesystem vulnerabilities, IaC misconfiguration, leaked secrets,
and dependency review on PRs.

Findings go to the GitHub Security tab via SARIF where possible, rather than only to the
job log. A finding in a log scrolls away after one push; a finding in the Security tab
stays until someone resolves or dismisses it, and dismissals are recorded.

`fail-on-severity` defaults to reporting rather than blocking. Turning a security scan
into a hard gate on day one, on a repo that has never been scanned, produces a red build
nobody can fix that afternoon — and the reliable outcome of that is the scan getting
disabled. Report first, triage the backlog, then tighten.

Usage:
  jobs:
    security:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/security-scan.yml@v1
      permissions:
        contents: read
        security-events: write
        pull-requests: read

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `filesystem-scan` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to scan dependencies and the filesystem for known CVEs. |
| `config-scan` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to scan IaC (Terraform, Dockerfile, Kubernetes) for misconfiguration. |
| `secret-scan` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to scan history for leaked credentials with gitleaks. |
| `dependency-review` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run GitHub dependency review on pull requests. |
| `image` | `string` | no | `""` | Container image reference to scan. Empty skips the image scan. |
| `severity` | `string` | no | `CRITICAL,HIGH` | Severities reported. |
| `fail-on-severity` | `string` | no | `""` | Severities that fail the build. Empty (default) reports without blocking. Set to `CRITICAL` once the backlog is triaged. |
| `ignore-unfixed` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to hide vulnerabilities with no available fix. |
| `trivyignore` | `string` | no | `.trivyignore` | Path to a `.trivyignore` file. |
| `upload-sarif` | `boolean` | no | `true` | 'true to upload SARIF to the Security tab. Needs `security-events: write`; silently unavailable on private repos without GitHub Advanced Security.' |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `20` | Per-job timeout. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GITLEAKS_LICENSE` | no | gitleaks-action licence key, required for organization repos. |

### Outputs

_No outputs._

## `terraform-ci`

Terraform CI — Terraform/OpenTofu CI: fmt, validate every root and example, tflint, trivy, and a

```yaml
jobs:
  terraform_ci:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/terraform-ci.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Terraform/OpenTofu CI: fmt, validate every root and example, tflint, trivy, and a
terraform-docs drift check. This is tf-tools' pipeline, generalised.

The validate job is the interesting one. `terraform validate` needs an initialised
directory, so it can't run once at the repo root — it has to run per module, per example,
and per environment. This workflow discovers those directories, honours a `.validate-skip`
marker for modules that wrap live third-party APIs and can't be validated offline, and
fans them out across a matrix so a 30-module monorepo doesn't validate serially.

Usage:
  jobs:
    ci:
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/terraform-ci.yml@v1
      with:
        directories: 'modules environments'

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary` | `string` | no | `terraform` | terraform \| tofu |
| `version` | `string` | no | `auto` | Version, or `auto` to read `.terraform-version` / `.opentofu-version`. |
| `directories` | `string` | no | `modules environments` | Space-separated roots searched for `.tf` files. |
| `skip-marker` | `string` | no | `.validate-skip` | A directory containing this file is excluded from validate. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `fmt` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run `fmt -check -recursive`. |
| `validate` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to init (no backend) and validate every discovered directory. |
| `tflint` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run tflint. |
| `tflint-version` | `string` | no | `latest` | tflint version. |
| `trivy` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to run a trivy config scan. |
| `trivy-severity` | `string` | no | `CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM` | Severities reported by trivy. |
| `trivy-fail` | `boolean` | no | `false` | `true` fails the build on findings. Default `false` matches tf-tools — report while the repo matures, then tighten. |
| `docs-check` | `boolean` | no | `false` | true to regenerate terraform-docs tables and fail if they drift. |
| `docs-directories` | `string` | no | `modules` | Root searched for modules needing docs (each dir with a `versions.tf`). |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `15` | Per-job timeout. |

### Outputs

_No outputs._

## `terraform-plan-apply`

Terraform plan/apply — Terraform plan on PRs, apply on merge — the standard GitOps loop, with the plan artifact

```yaml
jobs:
  terraform_plan_apply:
    uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/terraform-plan-apply.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit
```

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Terraform plan on PRs, apply on merge — the standard GitOps loop, with the plan artifact
carried between them.

The two halves are one workflow because the contract between them matters: the apply job
downloads and applies *the same binary plan* the reviewer approved. If it re-planned, the
thing that ran would not be the thing that was reviewed, and the PR comment would be
decoration rather than a gate.

`mode` selects the half:
  plan  → plan every changed root, comment the diff, upload the plan artifacts
  apply → download the artifacts and apply them
  both  → plan then apply in one run (for a `workflow_dispatch` or a trunk-based repo)

Which roots run is discovered from the diff by default, so a monorepo with thirty
environments only plans the ones that changed. Set `directories` to override.

Usage:
  jobs:
    plan:
      if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
      uses: patrickisgreat/actions-toolkit/.github/workflows/terraform-plan-apply.yml@v1
      with:
        mode: plan
        root-glob: 'environments/**'
        aws-role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::1234:role/gha-plan
        aws-region: us-east-1
      permissions: { contents: read, pull-requests: write, id-token: write }

</details>

### Inputs

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `string` | no | `plan` | plan \| apply \| both |
| `binary` | `string` | no | `terraform` | terraform \| tofu |
| `version` | `string` | no | `auto` | Version, or `auto` to read the version file. |
| `directories` | `string` | no | `""` | JSON array of root directories to operate on. Empty discovers them from the diff using `root-glob` and `root-marker`. |
| `root-glob` | `string` | no | `environments/**` | Glob matched against changed files during discovery. |
| `root-marker` | `string` | no | `main.tf` | File that marks a directory as a Terraform root during discovery. |
| `backend-config` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `key=value` backend settings or `.hcl` paths. |
| `var-files` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `.tfvars` paths. |
| `vars` | `string` | no | `""` | Newline-separated `key=value` variables. |
| `workspace` | `string` | no | `""` | Workspace to select. |
| `artifact-prefix` | `string` | no | `tfplan` | Prefix for the uploaded plan artifacts. |
| `comment-on-pr` | `boolean` | no | `true` | true to post each plan as a sticky PR comment. |
| `fail-on-destroy` | `boolean` | no | `false` | 'true to fail the plan when it would destroy anything. Worth turning on for production roots — an unintended destroy is the expensive mistake here.' |
| `environment-name` | `string` | no | `""` | GitHub Environment gating the apply job. |
| `aws-region` | `string` | no | `""` | AWS region, when the backend or providers need AWS. |
| `aws-role-to-assume` | `string` | no | `""` | OIDC role ARN for AWS. |
| `gcp-workload-identity-provider` | `string` | no | `""` | WIF provider for GCP. |
| `gcp-service-account` | `string` | no | `""` | Service account to impersonate for GCP. |
| `runs-on` | `string` | no | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label. |
| `timeout-minutes` | `number` | no | `30` | Per-job timeout. |

### Secrets

| Secret | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TF_SECRET_VARS` | no | Newline-separated `key=value` Terraform variables passed as `-var`. Use this for anything that must not appear in `with:`. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK` | no | — |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK` | no | — |

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| `directories` | JSON array of the roots that were planned. |
| `has-changes` | `true` if any root had changes. |
